# Smallest useful actual DuckDB C API v2 boundary

2026-11-01 UTC · **PRIMARY-SOURCE RESEARCH ONLY — NO ADAPTER OR EXECUTION PLAN**

## Finding

**The narrowest useful boundary supported by the inspected pin is a single-thread leaf table-function scan of one immutable, completed, owned reducer outcome.** It is an egress boundary: owned canonical project rows become typed DuckDB result rows only after the reducer outcome is complete. It is **not** a new SQL aggregate, a callback that consumes arbitrary SQL child tables, or proof of host compatibility. The underlying source basis is an actual v2 table builder requiring bind and exec callbacks and installing a producer scan, with constant bind arguments and a default one-thread scan state. This conclusion is a research inference from pinned declarations and implementation, not an implemented/selected interface. [Pinned table builder](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_table.cpp#L782-L837), [constant bind arguments](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb/main/capi_v2/capi_v2_function_internal.hpp#L121-L135), [scan-state default](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_table.cpp#L52-L63).

All count/min/max/final-mathematical-i64-sum results can conceptually use this same producer boundary. That does not establish that the standalone implementation produces a correct outcome, that a proposed SQL carrier is correct, or that the host can yet invoke the component. If the desired feature is **arbitrary SQL table → reducer in one SQL call**, this minimal egress boundary is expressly insufficient.

## 1. Exact pin, actual v2, no stability substitution

The exact requested ref `d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa` was verified by read-only public GitHub file retrieval. `duckdb_v2.h` returned blob `c36fe3ac3edd536aba8e79f6d7d9a81ed834c5e4`; the v2 extension header returned `b77dc115c1013e8f4db54f372cfd53d3148455ce`. Initial public web raw/blob routes cache-missed; no current/stable header was substituted. Full retrieval provenance and exact source identities are in `PINNED-EVIDENCE.md`.

The public header declares API **2.0.0**, gates the unstable surface, and warns that unstable constructs can change or disappear. The extension header has no stabilized v2 function surface and rejects mixing the v1/v2 extension-header families. This is an API-version/source finding, not an installed library version, release guarantee, extension-load result, or future ABI promise. [Version/surface declarations](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L66-L121), [actual v2 extension-family boundary](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_extension_v2.h#L14-L78).

## 2. What the minimal boundary means

| Responsibility | Conditional minimal scope | Explicit exclusion / prerequisite |
|---|---|---|
| Component input | One independently owned, completed typed request, supplied outside the producer's SQL-child path | The table callback is not an extractor/completion certificate for Datalog, temporal history, or arbitrary SQL relations. |
| Component outcome | One complete owned Success or Failure; no source/group is exposed while reduction is unfinished | Failure must not be turned into a successful empty relation or SQL NULL. |
| Binding | Immutable request/outcome identity plus a concrete output schema | Request lookup/transport, identity, access control, repeated binding and prepared-call lifetime are new interface decisions, not selected here. |
| Scan lifetime | Immutable owned rows retained for the bound call; separate per-execution cursor/state | Bound-data copies share the opaque owner at this pin; a mutable cursor must not be confused with immutable bind data. |
| Exec callback | Copies the next portion of an already complete result into callback-borrowed output vectors | No host SQL, input extraction, partial aggregate merge, optimizer hook, or temporal/store authority is assumed. |
| Concurrency | The v2 scan's one-thread default suffices for this boundary | No additional thread permission, parallel partition protocol, or synchronization correctness is inferred. |
| Optimizer interaction | No accepted filter predicates and no projection-pushdown obligation in the minimum | Claims about partitioning, ordering optimizations, or exact cardinality must be true and separately chosen. |

The public bind surface declares concrete result columns, at least one; `ANY` is not a data-bearing result type. Output chunks begin empty, are borrowed only for the callback, and use the first vector's size for produced row count; zero rows signals scan exhaustion. This naturally permits zero-row empty extrema versus a one-row zero for empty global count/sum. [Result-column requirements](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L12909-L12928), [actual output bridge/cardinality](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_table.cpp#L581-L625), [callback output lifetime](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L13289-L13308).

A host-invoking variant could associate a fresh owned request/result with scan-global initialization, provided completion/failure precedes every output batch. That is a **larger feasibility option**, not selected timing, an adapter design, or an execution plan. It adds per-execution ownership/copy/reset and interruption questions. Precomputed-result egress alone does not answer them.

## 3. Actual callback families are not interchangeable

| Actual public family | Pinned exposure | Consequence for the current component |
|---|---|---|
| Table function | Bind, global/local init, exec and optional progress/filter/partition hooks; the inspected builder installs a leaf producer | Fits owned completed rows and variable result cardinality. No exposed in-out SQL-child chunk callback was found in this builder; this is a bounded negative, not a claim about all DuckDB internals/APIs. |
| Scalar function | Bind/resolve/init plus vector-row exec; exec receives input argument vectors and a result vector | Not a whole-relation completion boundary. A list/struct-valued wrapper would be a new signature/carrier, not automatic aggregation or no-row extrema semantics. |
| Aggregate function | Size/init/update/**combine**/finalize and optional destroy; finalize has a result offset; update supplies row/state arrays | A direct adapter requires a new partial-state/disjoint-support/full-tuple-dedup/error-order contract. A mandatory combine cannot be inferred from the standalone reducer's final exact sum. |

The scalar source passes the current chunk/result vector, not a certified completed relation. The aggregate builder requires combine; its update bridge exports one state pointer per row, and finalize addresses `offset+i`. Arrays/borrowed vectors are not independent owned requests. The destroy path ignores a reported error, so cleanup cannot rely on reporting one. [Scalar exec bridge](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_scalar.cpp#L201-L232), [aggregate requirement](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_aggregate.cpp#L333-L375), [state/update/finalize/destruction bridge](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_aggregate.cpp#L223-L312).

SQL aggregate semantics are not a replacement specification: official documentation says general aggregates usually ignore NULL and, except count, return NULL on empty groups. Those docs are background, not an exact-pin execution result. The project's global-empty sum0 and no-row extrema therefore need explicit mapping. Likewise measure-DISTINCT does not preserve the project's full-source-tuple identity. [Official SQL aggregate semantics](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/functions/aggregates#handling-null-values).

## 4. Concrete typed vectors and a full-value carrier prerequisite

A DuckDB result column has a concrete type, while a project key/value position may contain different admitted tags on different rows. A native fixed primitive schema is useful only for an explicitly narrower, homogeneous-per-column subset. It does **not** cover the entire component domain or per-group extrema with differing measure tags.

One concrete **unselected carrier candidate** for the full domain is a four-member tagged SQL UNION: string bytes as BLOB, Boolean as BOOLEAN, i64 as BIGINT, and the canonical finite binary64 **word** as UBIGINT. A tagged STRUCT is another possible carrier, with an additional one-active-payload invariant. These are transport candidates, not newly selected SQL/API identities. The pinned API declares the necessary primitive/nested kinds, parameterized type construction, and UNION tag/member children. [Type construction](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L8953-L9068), [nested-vector children](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L11700-L11739).

Official UNION documentation confirms tagged alternatives, including a potentially NULL active payload, and implicit casts. Consequently an explicit non-NULL/tag/type/payload admission rule is still necessary; inferred coercion must not decide a project tag. SQL comparison on such a carrier is not a proof of the project's comparator. [Official UNION semantics, background only](https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/sql/data_types/union).

For exact f64 transport, the UBIGINT-word candidate avoids a decimal conversion or treating the C API's `double` argument as an already-proved portable interchange-word boundary. It does not change project finiteness/zero canonicalization or add floating sum. Native DOUBLE presentation remains a separate unverified mapping. Count/sum results remain i64 only **after** the final mathematical range check; host casts, NULL, saturation, or a wider successful SQL integer are not the same result. The public numeric getters may cast mismatched input types, as the actual `ReadAs` helper confirms: check concrete types/validity rather than treating a successful getter as strict tagged admission. [Cast-capable payload helper](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_value.cpp#L55-L83), [C double constructor](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_value.cpp#L548-L553).

## 5. Input/output ownership and validity

- **Input/ingress is separate.** Outside callbacks, v2 result stepping/fetching yields caller-owned chunks; vectors/views are borrowed from those chunks. Retaining a result chunk is not itself conversion into the component's closed owned tuple/string request. A later ingress boundary must preserve full source rows, transport raw order, validate all copies/unused fields, and separately account for extraction/copies. A single chunk or successful bind is not completed-relation evidence. [Owned result chunks and terminal statuses](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L12148-L12225).
- **Views are representation-aware.** The pinned vector source uses identity selection for flat storage, zero selection for constants, and dictionary selection into a child. Payload/validity indexing must honor that selection. A dictionary view can flatten a shared child and invalidate previously borrowed pointers through aliases. No unconditional flat-buffer or alias-safety assumption is justified. A single-cell copied value is a correctness fallback, not a throughput claim. [Actual view construction](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_vector.cpp#L144-L194), [copied cell read](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_vector.cpp#L428-L441).
- **Validity is semantic data.** Project values have no NULL arm. An outer NULL cell or NULL active carrier member cannot silently disappear. Default scalar/aggregate NULL handling can skip rows; explicit strict admission must not rely on that default. Nested raw validity writes must also preserve DuckDB's parent/descendant invariants. [Function NULL properties](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L691-L743), [nested validity obligations](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L11612-L11656).
- **Bytes need their own owner.** Host views are length-delimited and may contain interior NUL. Project strings still require their stricter NUL-free domain. Output variable-size payloads must belong to/copied into host-owned storage, not borrow a project string that can expire. The vector arena is borrowed and invalidated by flatten/reallocation/destruction; the fallback cell writer copies a value but also casts to the target type. [Byte/string views](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L446-L485), [output writer contract](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L11439-L11483), [arena lifetime](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L11679-L11695).
- **Binding is not a cursor.** Pinned bound-data copies share the opaque owner; the scan-global state is a different lifetime. Immutable rows and per-execution mutable positions require separate ownership. No output-owner/destructor safety was empirically established. [Bind-data sharing](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_table.cpp#L18-L48), [scan-global state ownership](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_table.cpp#L447-L478).

## 6. Errors, interruption, pushdown

V2 uses return codes plus optional owned error detail for ordinary API calls; success may leave stale detail untouched, so the return code is authoritative. Callback bridges supply a live borrowed error object, then translate its non-success code into the engine error path: it must not be destroyed/retained as if it were an ordinary caller-owned returned error handle. Callback context is also scope-borrowed, not a saved connection. A project structured error/counter carrier does not automatically fit that host channel. Fixed bounded project errors must not become successful SQL NULL/empty results; exact mapping, preservation of the owned outcome, allocation-failure handling and nonthrowing cleanup remain prerequisites. [Authoritative return-code/error wrapper](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb/main/capi_v2/capi_v2_internal.hpp#L756-L837), [table callback error propagation](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/main/capi/v2/capi_v2_func_table.cpp#L607-L614), [borrowed callback context](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L343-L352).

Connection interruption is publicly exposed, including cross-thread cancellation on the same connection. Stepping reports CANCELLED; blocking chunk fetch reports a runtime-interrupt error. That is **not** permission to start a thread, nor a demonstrated interruption/latency guarantee for a monolithic native reduction. No callback polling API was found in the inspected public v2 header; that is a bounded source finding, not a global claim about DuckDB internals. [Public cancellation contract](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L2001-L2019), [result statuses](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L12169-L12213).

Projection pushdown defaults false. Filter acceptance is a promise to implement the predicate exactly, because the engine stops applying accepted predicates; optimization can repeat the callback. For the minimum boundary, leaving these optional responsibilities unclaimed avoids confusing SQL output projection/filtering with the reducer's full-source contribution identity. Pushing a measure projection below deduplication or filtering contributions before reduction is not justified. [Exact pushdown responsibility](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L12807-L12854).

**Two separate atomicity boundaries:** the reducer can complete before its first host row, but DuckDB streams owned chunks. A later host transport/allocation/query error cannot be assumed to retract chunks already observed by a consumer. End-to-end all-or-nothing client visibility is an additional contract, not inherited from reducer atomicity. Similarly, canonical native row order is not a promise about every downstream SQL plan. These are research inferences from the stream/cardinality surface, not reproduced failures. [Streaming ownership/error contract](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L12148-L12225), [order metadata](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/blob/d54cbbe3df17e8e5ce68312f483b4155836112aa/src/include/duckdb_v2.h#L12952-L12974).

## Conclusion

Pinned source supports **conditional leaf-egress feasibility**, with explicit typed-carrier, owner, isolation and error prerequisites. It does not establish an integrated host feature, direct aggregate compatibility, arbitrary relation ingress, exact SQL agreement, interruption responsiveness, spilling, old compatibility, or performance. `RISKS-AND-OPEN-CLAIMS.md` lists the remaining decisions and one narrow pinned documentation/source discrepancy. No runtime/compile/import/probe, adapter implementation, execution plan, or external write occurred.
